newsitem.title: SPAIN: EU defense arm urges Albania diplomacy, not force.
newsitem.headline: EU defense arm urges Albania diplomacy, not force.

text.p: Europe's fledgling defence arm, the Western European Union (WEU), urged member states on Tuesday to seek a diplomatic rather than military solution to the crisis in Albania.
"It's not time to talk about Albania," WEU assembly president Lluis Maria de Puig told a news conference in Madrid. "It's time to try to resolve it through diplomatic avenues."

De Puig, in the Spanish capital for a WEU assembly meeting, said it was early days to discuss the use of outside force in Albania, which is under a state of emergency after riots by people enraged by the collapse of risky investment funds.
"We're not yet in a phase of sending a message through military intervention," he said.
In addition, de Puig said the 10-member WEU itself was not prepared to intervene because the conflict could potentially embroil two of its member states: Italy and Greece.

The WEU is empowered under a 1954 treaty to undertake military missions, but the grouping has changed its focus since the fall of the Berlin wall and is still working out the best way to coordinate new challenges such as the Albania crisis.
"The question is which country leads the force," de Puig said. "It's a European matter that needs to be resolved...what to do if we have a member country involved."
